fields.value: Section 14 describes a GLP-1 agonist (for example, exenatide) 5 mcg subcutaneously within 60 minutes before infusion, intended to continue at 5 mcg twice daily for up to 6 months after transplant. The first four Study 1 subjects did not receive exenatide; 11 of the remaining 26 used it for less than 6 months because of adverse reactions. The reactions and finer breakdown of those 11 are not specified.

fields.value: Section 5.1 states concomitant immunosuppression is required to maintain islet viability and describes risks including bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic infections; lymphomas and other malignancies, particularly skin cancer; and severe anemia, sometimes requiring transfusion. It also describes vaccination, prophylaxis, monitoring, and potential discontinuation circumstances. Section 14 Table 3 source-reported medication counts and percentages (Study 1 N=10; Study 2 N=20): anakinra 1 (10%) / 0 (0%); daclizumab 10 (100%) / 5 (24%); basiliximab 5 (10%) / 19 (95%); mycophenolate mofetil 6 (60%) / 5 (24%); etanercept 6 (60%) / 20 (100%); everolimus 1 (10%) / 2 (10%); sirolimus 10 (100%) / 20 (100%); tacrolimus 10 (100%) / 20 (100%); cyclosporine 1 (10%) / 3 (15%); anti-thymocyte immunoglobulin 1 (10%) / 4 (20%).

fields.value: LANTIDRA is a suspension/cellular product of allogeneic pancreatic islets (islets of Langerhans) derived from a donor pancreas. The product is supplied in buffered transplant medium with HEPES and human serum albumin; a separate rinse bag contains transplant medium.

fields.value: Section 2.1 says a second infusion may be performed if independence from exogenous insulin is not achieved within one year of infusion, or within one year after loss of independence following a prior infusion; a third may use the same criteria. Section 6.1 reports intervals between first and second transplants of 1 month–2.8 years and between second and third doses of 3 months–7.8 years. Figure 1 sets time zero at the first infusion.
